title: Marketplace package manifest
description: The unit of publication. A manifest is signed as a whole (signature.schema.json) and the signature transitively covers the payload because `payload.digest` is a digest over (relative_path, sha256) for every payload file. Spec 10846-10871 requires versions+channels, dependency metadata, platform/client compatibility, permissions, provenance, SBOM, license metadata, quality score, benchmark evidence and deprecation -- all of them live here or are $ref'd from here, so there is exactly ONE place a publisher declares a fact about a package.

kind.description: Artifact class. Closed set: the resolver dispatches on it, so an unknown kind must be a validation failure and not a runtime surprise.

notice_required.description: True for Apache-2.0-family terms that require NOTICE preservation. The linter cross-checks this against the per-file licences in the SBOM: TOURNAMENT-VERDICT.md M1 records 31 Apache-2.0 payload entries aggregated under a declared MIT in this very repo, which is exactly the defect this field plus MKT-L03 detects.

aggregate_verified.description: The publisher asserts the declared SPDX is compatible with EVERY component licence in the SBOM. `false` is publishable to a private mirror but MKT-L04 refuses a public publish.

permissions.description: The COMPLETE set the package may use. Deny-by-default: anything not listed is refused at install time, and anything listed that the trust policy does not grant refuses the install.

files.description: EXPLICIT allowlist. There is no glob and no implicit `**`: marketplace-first FM-4 measured an absolute local path leaking through a committed registry row, and an enumerated payload is the only form a reviewer can read.

receipt_ref.description: Optional pointer to the Wave-1 completion receipt that certified the payload. This is the ACCEPTANCE plane of marketplace-first 1.5 -- publishing is gated on the 12-condition predicate that already exists rather than on a new one.

deprecation.description: DEPRECATION is advisory: install warns and proceeds. REVOCATION (revocation.schema.json) is enforcement: install refuses. Conflating the two is how a revocation becomes a warning nobody reads.

signature.description: Publisher signature over the canonical form of this manifest with `signature` removed, domain `mkt.manifest.v1`. Absent in an UNSIGNED draft (the scaffolder emits one); required by every consumer -- `trust-policy.on_missing.signature` is a one-value enum so a build in which an unsigned package installs is not expressible.
